204	returns jsonb
205	language plpgsql
206	security invoker
207	set search_path = ''
208	as $fn$
209	declare
210	  v_out jsonb;
211	begin
212	  if p_claim is null or char_length(p_claim) not between 8 and 64 or p_lease_sec is null or p_lease_sec < 30 then
213	    raise exception 'claim_invalid' using errcode = '22023';
214	  end if;
215	
216	  with picked as (
217	    select d.id, d.status as was
218	      from public.alert_deliveries d
219	     where (d.channel_id is null or exists (select 1 from public.alert_channels c where c.id=d.channel_id and c.kind in ('email','telegram')))
220	       and (p_event_id is null or d.event_id = p_event_id)
221	       and ((d.status = 'pending' and d.next_at <= now())
222	            or (d.status = 'sending' and d.claimed_at < now() - make_interval(secs => p_lease_sec)))
223	       and (d.event <> 'resolved' or not exists (
224	             select 1 from public.alert_deliveries o
225	              where o.incident_id = d.incident_id and o.event = 'opened' and o.channel_id is not distinct from d.channel_id
226	                and o.recipient = d.recipient and o.status in ('pending', 'sending')))
227	     order by d.created_at, d.id
228	     limit greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_limit, 10), 100))
229	       for update of d skip locked
230	  ),
231	  claimed as (
232	    update public.alert_deliveries d
233	       set status = 'sending', claim = p_claim, claimed_at = clock_timestamp(), attempts = least(d.attempts + 1, 100)
234	      from picked p
235	     where d.id = p.id
236	    returning d.*, p.was
237	  )
238	  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
239	           'id', d.id, 'event', d.event, 'eventId', d.event_id, 'attempts', d.attempts, 'inDoubt', d.was = 'sending',
240	           'recipient', d.recipient, 'workspaceId', d.workspace_id, 'clerkOrgId', w.clerk_org_id,
241	           'createdAt', d.created_at,
242	           'channel', case when c.id is null then null
243	                           else jsonb_build_object('id', c.id, 'kind', c.kind, 'audience', c.audience, 'address', c.address,
244	                                                   'chatId', c.chat_id::text) end,
245	           'why', case when c.id is null then 'channel_removed'
246	                       when c.unsubscribed_at is not null
247	                         or exists (select 1 from public.alert_suppressions s where s.channel_id = c.id and s.recipient = d.recipient) then 'unsubscribed'
248	                       when c.confirmed_at is null then 'unconfirmed'
249	                       when d.event <> 'test'
250	                         and not public.alert_route_matches(c.id, d.incident_id) then 'excluded'
251	                  end,
252	           'stateAfter', e.state_after,
253	           'incident', case when i.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object(
254	             'id', i.id, 'title', i.title, 'severity', i.severity, 'openedAt', i.opened_at, 'resolvedAt', i.resolved_at,
255	             'evidence', i.evidence) end,
256	           'monitor', case when m.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object('id', m.id, 'name', m.name, 'type', m.type) end,
257	           'app', case when a.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object('id', a.id, 'name', a.name) end,
258	           'pageSlug', (select p.slug from public.status_pages p where p.app_id = a.id)
259	         ) order by d.created_at, d.id), '[]'::jsonb)
260	    into v_out
261	    from claimed d
262	    join public.workspaces w on w.id = d.workspace_id
263	    join public.alert_events e on e.id = d.event_id
264	    left join public.alert_channels c on c.id = d.channel_id
265	    left join public.incidents i on i.id = d.incident_id
266	    left join public.monitors m on m.id = i.monitor_id
267	    left join public.apps a on a.id = m.app_id;

270	end;

  )
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
           'id', d.id, 'event', d.event, 'eventId', d.event_id, 'attempts', d.attempts, 'inDoubt', d.was = 'sending',
           'recipient', d.recipient, 'workspaceId', d.workspace_id, 'clerkOrgId', w.clerk_org_id,
           'createdAt', d.created_at,
           'channel', case when c.id is null then null
                           else jsonb_build_object('id', c.id, 'kind', c.kind, 'audience', c.audience, 'address', c.address,
                                                   'chatId', c.chat_id::text) end,
           'why', case when c.id is null then 'channel_removed'
                       when c.unsubscribed_at is not null
                         or exists (select 1 from public.alert_suppressions s where s.channel_id = c.id and s.recipient = d.recipient) then 'unsubscribed'
                       when c.confirmed_at is null then 'unconfirmed'
                       when d.event <> 'test'
                         and not public.alert_route_matches(c.id, d.incident_id) then 'excluded'
                  end,
           'stateAfter', e.state_after,
           'incident', case when i.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object(
             'id', i.id, 'title', i.title, 'severity', i.severity, 'openedAt', i.opened_at, 'resolvedAt', i.resolved_at,
             'evidence', i.evidence) end,
           'monitor', case when m.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object('id', m.id, 'name', m.name, 'type', m.type) end,
           'app', case when a.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object('id', a.id, 'name', a.name) end,
           'pageSlug', (select p.slug from public.status_pages p where p.app_id = a.id)
         ) order by d.created_at, d.id), '[]'::jsonb)
    into v_out
    from claimed d
    join public.workspaces w on w.id = d.workspace_id
    join public.alert_events e on e.id = d.event_id
    left join public.alert_channels c on c.id = d.channel_id
    left join public.incidents i on i.id = d.incident_id
    left join public.monitors m on m.id = i.monitor_id
    left join public.apps a on a.id = m.app_id;

  return v_out;
end;
$fn$;

create or replace function public.alert_claim_channels(p_claim text, p_limit integer, p_lease_sec integer, p_event_id text)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security invoker
set search_path = ''
as $fn$
declare
  v_out jsonb;
begin
  if p_claim is null or char_length(p_claim) not between 8 and 64 or p_lease_sec is null or p_lease_sec < 30 then
    raise exception 'claim_invalid' using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  with picked as (
    select d.id, d.status as was
      from public.alert_deliveries d
     where (p_event_id is null or d.event_id = p_event_id)
       and ((d.status = 'pending' and d.next_at <= now())
            or (d.status = 'sending' and d.claimed_at < now() - make_interval(secs => p_lease_sec)))
       and (d.event <> 'resolved' or not exists (
             select 1 from public.alert_deliveries o
              where o.incident_id = d.incident_id and o.event = 'opened' and o.channel_id is not distinct from d.channel_id
                and o.recipient = d.recipient and o.status in ('pending', 'sending')))
     order by d.created_at, d.id
     limit greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_limit, 10), 100))
       for update of d skip locked
  ),
  claimed as (
    update public.alert_deliveries d
       set status = 'sending', claim = p_claim, claimed_at = clock_timestamp(), attempts = least(d.attempts + 1, 100)
      from picked p
     where d.id = p.id
    returning d.*, p.was
  )
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
           'id', d.id, 'event', d.event, 'eventId', d.event_id, 'attempts', d.attempts, 'inDoubt', d.was = 'sending',
           'recipient', d.recipient, 'workspaceId', d.workspace_id, 'clerkOrgId', w.clerk_org_id,
           'createdAt', d.created_at, 'webhookStartedAt', d.webhook_started_at, 'webhookBody', d.webhook_body, 'webhookAttempts', d.webhook_attempts,
           'parentProviderId', (select o.provider_id from public.alert_deliveries o where o.incident_id=d.incident_id and o.channel_id=d.channel_id and o.event='opened' and o.status='sent' limit 1),
           'channel', case when c.id is null then null
                           else jsonb_build_object('id', c.id, 'kind', c.kind, 'audience', c.audience, 'address', c.address,
                                                   'chatId', c.chat_id::text, 'sealed', c.sealed) end,
           'why', case when c.id is null then 'channel_removed'
                       when c.unsubscribed_at is not null
                         or exists (select 1 from public.alert_suppressions s where s.channel_id = c.id and s.recipient = d.recipient) then 'unsubscribed'
                       when c.confirmed_at is null then 'unconfirmed'
                       when d.event <> 'test'
                         and not public.alert_route_matches(c.id, d.incident_id) then 'excluded'
                  end,
           'stateAfter', e.state_after,
           'incident', case when i.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object(
             'id', i.id, 'title', i.title, 'severity', i.severity, 'openedAt', i.opened_at, 'resolvedAt', i.resolved_at,
             'evidence', i.evidence) end,
           'monitor', case when m.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object('id', m.id, 'name', m.name, 'type', m.type) end,
           'app', case when a.id is null then null else jsonb_build_object('id', a.id, 'name', a.name) end,
           'pageSlug', (select p.slug from public.status_pages p where p.app_id = a.id)
         ) order by d.created_at, d.id), '[]'::jsonb)
    into v_out
    from claimed d
    join public.workspaces w on w.id = d.workspace_id
    join public.alert_events e on e.id = d.event_id
    left join public.alert_channels c on c.id = d.channel_id
    left join public.incidents i on i.id = d.incident_id
    left join public.monitors m on m.id = i.monitor_id
    left join public.apps a on a.id = m.app_id;

  return v_out;
end;
$fn$;

create or replace function public.alert_prepare_webhook(p_id text, p_claim text, p_body text)
returns jsonb language plpgsql security invoker set search_path = '' as $fn$
declare d public.alert_deliveries;
begin
  if p_body is null or octet_length(p_body) > 16384 then raise exception 'payload_invalid' using errcode='22023'; end if;
  update public.alert_deliveries set webhook_body=coalesce(webhook_body,p_body), webhook_started_at=coalesce(webhook_started_at,clock_timestamp()), webhook_attempts=webhook_attempts+1
    where id=p_id and claim=p_claim and status='sending' and webhook_attempts<6 and exists(select 1 from public.alert_channels c where c.id=channel_id and c.kind='webhook')
    returning * into d;
  if not found then return null; end if;
  return jsonb_build_object('body',d.webhook_body,'startedAt',d.webhook_started_at,'attempts',d.webhook_attempts);
end;
$fn$;

create or replace function alert_sender.alert_claim_channels(p_claim text,p_limit integer,p_lease_sec integer,p_event_id text)
returns jsonb language sql security definer set search_path = '' as $fn$
  select public.alert_claim_channels(p_claim,p_limit,p_lease_sec,p_event_id);
$fn$;
alter function alert_sender.alert_claim_channels(text,integer,integer,text) owner to postgres;
create or replace function alert_sender.alert_prepare_webhook(p_id text,p_claim text,p_body text)
returns jsonb language sql security definer set search_path = '' as $fn$
  select public.alert_prepare_webhook(p_id,p_claim,p_body);
$fn$;
alter function alert_sender.alert_prepare_webhook(text,text,text) owner to postgres;
revoke all on function alert_sender.alert_claim_channels(text,integer,integer,text), alert_sender.alert_prepare_webhook(text,text,text)
  from public,anon,authenticated,service_role,probe,ingest,watchdog,alert_sender;
grant execute on function alert_sender.alert_claim_channels(text,integer,integer,text), alert_sender.alert_prepare_webhook(text,text,text) to alert_sender;

To add Microsoft Teams, copy the Discord channel. Discord is the closest existing channel: the member pastes an incoming-webhook URL, it is encrypted ("sealed") into `alert_channels.sealed`, and the sender Worker posts to it with no OAuth step. The changes cover one SQL migration, about five files in `src/lib`, three dashboard files, tests and copy. Paths are relative to the clone at `<BENCH>\staygreen`, and nothing in the repo was changed.

## 1. Database: a new migration

**Add** `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_teams_channel.sql`. The project rule is never to edit applied migrations, only to add new ones (`docs/deploying.md:61`). In it:

1. **Allow the new kind.** Drop and re-add `alert_channels_kind_check` with `'teams'` added, the way migration 028 did (`supabase/migrations/20261023120000_alert_channels.sql:4-5`).
2. **Store the credential like other channels.** No change is needed: `alert_channels_built` already requires `sealed`, `confirmed_at` and `label` for every kind other than email and Telegram (`alert_channels.sql:6-8`).
3. **Re-create `public.alert_expand` in full,** with `'teams'` added to its hard-coded kind list. **Without this, no Teams receipt is ever created.** The current definition only creates receipts for `('email','telegram','slack','discord','webhook')` (`alert_channels.sql:132-201`, list at line 185).
4. **Nothing else.** `alert_claim_channels` doesn't filter by kind and already returns `sealed` (`alert_channels.sql:286-314`). The legacy `alert_claim` is email/Telegram only and stays that way (`alert_channels.sql:219`). The `alert_sender` wrappers and grants are unchanged.

## 2. Core library

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/alerts/channel-input.ts` | Add `teamsUrl()` next to `discordUrl()`. It builds on `webhookUrl()` (HTTPS, port 443, no login, no private hosts) and **allowlists the Microsoft hosts and path shape**, as `discordUrl` does for `discord.com` (`:15-21`). Add `"teams"` to `channelInput.kind` and its error message (`:23-34`). |
| `src/lib/alerts/providers.ts` | Add `sendTeams(url, message, doFetch)` modeled on `sendDiscord` (`:58-78`). Re-validate the URL; use `redirect: "manual"` and a 10 s timeout; build the body from `mask`ed text with a length cap that keeps the link footer, as `discordText` does (`:26-35`). Map responses to `SendResult`: 429 → `retry`, 4xx → `rejected`, anything uncertain → `unknown`, and `neverLeft` → `retry`. |
| `src/lib/alerts/sender.ts` | Add `"teams"` to the channel list in `deliver` (`:363`). Dispatch it like Discord (`:377`): `settle(d, await sendTeams(credential.url ?? "", message, deps.channels.fetch))`. Treat it like Slack/Discord in two places: when the provider never answered (`:272`, fail rather than send blind) and when a claim's lease expired (`:339`). |
| `src/lib/alerts/server.ts` | Add `"teams"` to the `ChannelView.kind` union (`:33`) and the zod enum (`:81`). Otherwise the dashboard snapshot fails to parse a Teams row. |
| `src/lib/model.ts` | Add `"teams"` to `ChannelKind` (`:217`). |

Two things are specific to Teams:
- **A `sent` receipt needs a provider id.** The database requires `provider_id` to be non-null when a receipt is `sent` (`supabase/migrations/20261022195510_alerts_email.sql:152`). Discord returns a message id (`providers.ts:72`). If the Teams endpoint returns only `202` with no body, `sendTeams` must supply a stable id, such as a request-id header or the delivery id.
- **Recoveries can't be threaded.** Slack posts a recovery as a reply in the opening message's thread (`sender.ts:374-375`). Teams webhooks can't, so recoveries go out as separate messages, as Discord's do.

No change is needed in `sender/worker.ts`. It already passes a `fetch` and `CREDENTIALS_KEY` to the channels (`sender/worker.ts:31`), and the encrypted credential is opened generically (`sender.ts:364-369`).

## 3. Dashboard

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/app/(app)/app/alerts/actions.ts` | In `addWebhookChannel` (`:276-295`), normalize the URL with `teamsUrl(v.url)!.href` (`:289`). Seal it with `channelContext` exactly as before. Add `"teams"` to the kinds whose test alert is queued rather than sent at once (`:223`). |
| `src/app/(app)/app/alerts/ChannelSettings.tsx` | Add `"teams"` to the `kind` state (`:18`), a "Microsoft Teams" button (`:47`), and the dialog title, field label and hint (`:54-59`). |
| `src/app/(app)/app/alerts/AlertsScreen.tsx` | Add a channel description (`:98`) and a receipt label such as "Teams message" (`:361`). |
| `src/components/alerts/ChannelIcon.tsx` | Add `teams` to `icons` and `kindName` (`:4,6`). This is a typed `Record<ChannelKind, …>`, so it won't compile after the `model.ts` change until you do. |

## 4. Tests

- `tests/unit/channels.test.ts`: URL validation, as in "allows only the provider's exact webhook path and host" (`:47-52`); the send body, masking and length cap (pattern at `:77-101`); and 429/uncertain mapping (`:103`).
- `tests/unit/channel-actions.test.ts`: the add-channel action for Teams.
- `tests/integration/channels.test.ts`: the database refuses unknown kinds, and `alert_expand` creates Teams receipts.
- `tests/e2e/channels.auth.spec.ts`: the dialog flow.

## 5. Copy and docs that list the channels

- `src/app/(public)/page.tsx:95` and `src/components/PlanTable.tsx:51`
- `src/app/(public)/legal/privacy/page.tsx:168`: Microsoft becomes a recipient of alert content.
- `scripts/clerk/billing.json:115`
- `docs/deploying.md:26` and `examples/sender/wrangler.toml:2,38`
- Optionally `src/lib/launch.ts:83-86`, if you want Teams hidden until it's switched on.

## 6. Deploy order

Each part is updated separately (`docs/deploying.md:70`):
1. Apply the migration with `supabase db push`.
2. Redeploy the sender Worker. The Worker imports `src/lib/alerts/sender.ts` and `providers.ts`, so it needs the new code.
3. Deploy the app.

Doing it in this order means a Teams channel can't be saved before its receipts can be created and sent.

**Check outside the repo:** which Teams URL format to accept. Microsoft has been replacing Office 365 connector webhooks with Power Automate "Workflows" webhooks, which use different hosts and expect an Adaptive Card body. Confirm the current hosts, path pattern, payload and response before writing `teamsUrl()` and `sendTeams()`. If the hosts can't be pinned to a fixed allowlist the way Discord's can, use the signed-webhook path instead. It checks that the hostname resolves only to public addresses (`actions.ts:284-287`), and sends through `pinnedWebhookTransport` (`src/lib/alerts/webhook.ts`), which connects only to the checked address, verifies TLS and never follows redirects (`tests/unit/channels.test.ts:164-169`).

"", message, deps.channels.fetch))`. Treat it like Slack/Discord in two places: when the provider never answered (`:272`, fail rather than send blind) and when a claim's lease expired (`:339`). |

Two things are specific to Teams:
- **A `sent` receipt needs a provider id.** The database requires `provider_id` to be non-null when a receipt is `sent` (`supabase/migrations/20261022195510_alerts_email.sql:152`). Discord returns a message id (`providers.ts:72`). If the Teams endpoint returns only `202` with no body, `sendTeams` must supply a stable id, such as a request-id header or the delivery id.
- **Recoveries can't be threaded.** Slack posts a recovery as a reply in the opening message's thread (`sender.ts:374-375`). Teams webhooks can't, so recoveries go out as separate messages, as Discord's do.

No change is needed in `sender/worker.ts`. It already passes a `fetch` and `CREDENTIALS_KEY` to the channels (`sender/worker.ts:31`), and the encrypted credential is opened generically (`sender.ts:364-369`).

## 6. Deploy order

Each part is updated separately (`docs/deploying.md:70`):
1. Apply the migration with `supabase db push`.
2. Redeploy the sender Worker. The Worker imports `src/lib/alerts/sender.ts` and `providers.ts`, so it needs the new code.
3. Deploy the app.

Doing it in this order means a Teams channel can't be saved before its receipts can be created and sent.

**Check outside the repo:** which Teams URL format to accept. Microsoft has been replacing Office 365 connector webhooks with Power Automate "Workflows" webhooks, which use different hosts and expect an Adaptive Card body. Confirm the current hosts, path pattern, payload and response before writing `teamsUrl()` and `sendTeams()`. If the hosts can't be pinned to a fixed allowlist the way Discord's can, use the signed-webhook path instead. It checks that the hostname resolves only to public addresses (`actions.ts:284-287`), and sends through `pinnedWebhookTransport` (`src/lib/alerts/webhook.ts`), which connects only to the checked address, verifies TLS and never follows redirects (`tests/unit/channels.test.ts:164-169`).
